restaurant_name: Dental Whizz Clinic - เดนทัลวิศ
text:
I initially visited the dentist because of a tooth problem. A middle-aged female dentist explained the overall treatment plan and pricing to me in advance:
root canal treatment 12,000 THB, post 5,000 THB, and crown 18,000 THB.
I later checked market prices myself and felt this pricing structure was reasonable, so I agreed to proceed.
The root canal treatment was then carried out by a younger female dentist over three visits. Each time, local anesthesia and a rubber dam were used. The treatment was careful and professional, and temporary fillings were placed after each visit.
I asked her when the permanent filling would be done, and she clearly told me it should be done after the post was completed. That made sense to me, so I agreed.
I later scheduled the post procedure with the middle-aged dentist.
Before the treatment, I clearly explained that I wanted to complete the post and permanent filling first, and consider the crown a few months later — partly to observe the result of the root canal, and partly for financial and personal decision-making reasons. The dentist did not object at that time.
On the day of the post procedure, no rubber dam was used, and the process took about 30 minutes.
During the treatment, I felt the dentist’s handling was quite rough. Several times the pain I felt was not from the tooth itself, but from physical discomfort caused by hand movements, which made me uncomfortable.
After the procedure, the dentist said it was finished and turned away. When I tested my bite myself, I noticed it was clearly uneven. After I pointed this out, she returned to adjust it and apologized for not smoothing it properly.
The issue arose at checkout.
In addition to the previously stated 5,000 THB for the post, an extra 3,000 THB was added to the bill, listed as a tooth-colored filling.
I questioned this immediately, as this charge had never been mentioned beforehand. The clinic staff explained that it was because “premium filling material” was used. I did not agree with this explanation, but since the dentist was introduced by a friend, I chose not to argue at the time and paid.
A few days later, the clinic contacted me again and repeated the same explanation, adding that I would receive a discount if I chose to do the crown with them in the future.
However, in my view, this did not address the core issue of inconsistent pricing before and after treatment, but instead shifted the problem to potential future treatment.
Personal note:
I have been living in Thailand for more than ten years and have visited many doctors and private hospitals during that time. My experience has generally been that pricing is transparent, service standards are high, and doctors are professional, respectful, and well-qualified.
Against that background, this experience was particularly disappointing.
I cannot judge whether this clinic or this dentist treats long-term, regular patients in the same way. However, if you are only planning short-term or stage-by-stage treatment (for example, stopping after the post and not proceeding immediately with a crown), I personally would not recommend this clinic, or at least would advise being extremely cautious and confirming all fees very clearly in advance.
